title: Chain of records with a front entry, read by walking
summary: Each written pair becomes a record with the index of the next record, and new records go to the front of the chain. Reading walks the chain from the front until a record with the wanted address. Removal unlinks that record. A three-mode controller decides what is written and read.
core_idea: Keep pairs as a front-inserted chain of records and walk it to read, under a searched three-mode controller.

state.name: Ra
state.meaning: Address of each record, in creation order.

state.name: Nx
state.meaning: Index of the next record in the chain, -1 at the end.

state.name: fr
state.meaning: Index of the front record, -1 when the chain is empty.

state.name: ctl
state.meaning: Controller registers: mode mu, stop symbol sigma, separators Z, answer set A, hop limit H, held token p, write flag w, position c, emitted count o, depth d; about 16 words plus |A| + |Z|.

state.name: M
state.meaning: Learned translation from a read result to an emitted symbol, at most N entries for an alphabet of N symbols.

update.latex:
x_t=\sigma \Rightarrow w\leftarrow 0,\, o\leftarrow 0;\quad \mu=0:\; x_t\in Z \Rightarrow p\leftarrow\varnothing;\; w=1,\, p=\varnothing \Rightarrow p\leftarrow x_t;\; w=1,\, p
eq\varnothing \Rightarrow \mathrm{ins}(p, x_t),\, p\leftarrow\varnothing;\quad \mu=1:\; w=1,\, x_t
otin Z \Rightarrow \mathrm{ins}(c, x_t),\, c\leftarrow c+1;\; w=0 \Rightarrow o\leftarrow o+1;\quad \mu=2:\; x_t\in A \Rightarrow \mathrm{del}(d, \mathrm{get}(d)),\, d\leftarrow d-1;\; x_t
otin A \Rightarrow d\leftarrow d+1,\, \mathrm{ins}(d, x_t)
update.plain: controller step: the stop symbol sigma ends writing; in pair mode a token waits in p or completes a pair that goes into the store with ins; in string mode each symbol goes in under the running position c; in nesting mode an opener goes in at the raised depth d and a closer takes out the entry at d
update.name: controller

update.latex: \mathrm{ins}(a,b):\; \text{new record } r = (a, b, fr),\; fr \leftarrow r
update.plain: ins creates a record pointing to the old front and makes it the front; a write that would exceed C entries is dropped
update.name: prepend

update.latex: \mathrm{del}(a,b):\; \text{walk from } fr;\; \text{relink the predecessor of the first record with address } a \text{ to its successor}
update.plain: del unlinks the first record whose address is a
update.name: unlink

readout.latex: \mu=0:\; y_0=x_t,\; r_j=\mathrm{get}(y_{j-1}),\; u=r_j \text{ at the first } j\le H \text{ with } r_j\in A,\; u=r_{j-1} \text{ at the first } r_j=\varnothing;\quad \mu=1:\; u=\mathrm{get}(o);\quad \mu=2:\; u=\mathrm{get}(d);\qquad \hat{y}_t = M[u] \text{ for } u\in\mathrm{dom}\,M,\; A_0 \text{ for } u=\varnothing,\; u \text{ otherwise}
readout.plain: read: in pair mode get what is held for the current token and keep following while the result is not in the answer set A, at most H times; in string mode get position o; in nesting mode get depth d; translate through M
readout.name: readout

readout.latex: \mathrm{get}(a):\; r \leftarrow fr;\; \text{while } r \ne -1 \text{ and } Ra_r \ne a: r \leftarrow Nx_r;\; \text{return } Rb_r \text{ or } \varnothing
readout.plain: get walks from the front record and returns the item of the first record with address a

learning.description: A finite search: the answer set A is collected from the training targets and the separator set Z from the symbols that occur exactly once in every training sequence. For each mode and each stop choice (none or a member of Z) the controller runs over the m sequences, the pairs (read result, target) are tallied, M takes the majority target per read result, and the setting with the highest training accuracy is kept.
learning.few_shot_argument: The space has at most 3(|Z| + 1) + 1 settings plus a majority map, so m = 12 sequences pick the right setting in the small cases (copy and recall at 4, depth 2, composition at 4, binding at 2) on three seeds.

complexity.constants_notes: A walk visits at most C records; at most H walks per token.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Search over a handful of controller settings with a majority translation.

prediction.statement: With m = 12 training examples the learned controller reaches accuracy at least 0.99 on copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, nesting at depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops, on three seeds.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: String mode with C = L copies L = 8, 32, 64 over D = 4 with per-string accuracy 1.0 within 6C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = K and H = 1 answers K = 8, 32, 64 with per-query accuracy 1.0 within 6C + N + 16 words (N = 2K + 17 at K = 64 with V = 16).
Nesting mode with C = depth predicts the legal closer at depth 2, 4, 8, 16 with accuracy 1.0 within 6C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2T and H = 2 answers f(g(x)) at T = 4, 16, 32 with accuracy 1.0 within 6C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2(hops + 1) and H = hops + 1 resolves chains of 1, 4, 8 hops with accuracy 1.0 within 6C + N + 16 words.
The search learner reaches 0.99 from m = 12 examples on seeds 0, 1, 2 for copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops.

For any fixed capacity C, recall of K = C + 1 distinct pairs over V = 16 symbols fails on some instance: the store holds at most C pairs, so one probe's item is absent and is answered from at most 16 guesses (at C = 64 this is K = 65, above every P2 size).

toy_example.description: Three records, a fetch that sees the newest of two equal addresses, and an unlink.
